primitives.name: TamperEvidentAuditLog
primitives.purpose: Append-only record of security-relevant events, hash-chained and signed so any retroactive mutation is detectable by verification.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Any

class TamperEvidentAuditLog(Protocol):
    def append(self, actor: str, action: str, resource: str, outcome: str, attributes: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str: ...
    def verify_chain(self, start_seq: int | None = None, end_seq: int | None = None) -> bool: ...
    def get(self, seq: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def export(self, since_seq: int) -> bytes: ...
invariants: Entries MUST be append-only; the store SHALL reject UPDATE or DELETE on any prior sequence.
Each entry MUST contain the SHA-256 of the prior entry, forming a chain that CANNOT be mutated without detection.
Each entry MUST carry a signature from a key whose private half is NEVER held by the writing service.
Sequence numbers MUST be monotonically increasing with no gaps; verify_chain SHALL fail on gap or regression.
Actor, action, resource, outcome, and timestamp MUST be present on every entry; absence SHALL raise.
Clock source MUST be monotonic server-side; client-supplied timestamps SHALL be rejected.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream targets register a signer adapter (KMS/HSM) and a storage backend (object-lock S3, WORM volume, ledger DB) by implementing the TamperEvidentAuditLog Protocol. Additional attribute fields compose via an attribute-enrichment hook invoked before signing.
primitives.consumption_example:
def record_admin_reset(log: TamperEvidentAuditLog, admin_id: str, user_id: str) -> None:
    seq = log.append(
        actor=admin_id,
        action='user.password_reset',
        resource=f'user:{user_id}',
        outcome='success',
        attributes={'via': 'admin_console'},
    )
    assert log.verify_chain(end_seq=None) is True, 'audit chain broke'

primitives.why_essential: Without a shared chain-verified log, each tool writes its own audit stream and regulators cannot prove evidence integrity; a centralized primitive forces one signed chain per tenant.
alternatives_considered: Per-table shadow columns (updated_by, updated_at) — trivially tamperable by DBA and fails CC7.2 non-repudiation.
Database binlog replay — captures DML but not business actor/outcome and is not signed.
Application log aggregation to SIEM only — breaks on SIEM outage and has no chain verification.

primitives.name: RetentionPolicy
primitives.purpose: Declarative binding of a data class to a maximum lifetime, enforced by scheduled purge and blocked at write-time if unclassified.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RetentionPolicy:
    data_class: str
    max_age: timedelta
    legal_basis: str
    deletion_mode: str  # 'hard' | 'crypto_shred' | 'anonymize'

class RetentionEnforcer(Protocol):
    def bind(self, policy: RetentionPolicy) -> None: ...
    def enforce_on_write(self, data_class: str, record_id: str) -> None: ...
    def sweep(self) -> int: ...
invariants: Every persisted record MUST be tagged with a data_class that maps to a registered RetentionPolicy; writes of untagged data SHALL be rejected.
max_age MUST be finite and > 0; an open-ended 'keep forever' policy CANNOT be registered without an explicit legal_basis override.
deletion_mode MUST be one of 'hard', 'crypto_shred', or 'anonymize'; other values SHALL raise on bind.
The sweep job MUST be idempotent and SHALL not delete records under an active LegalHold.
Every purge action MUST emit an entry to the TamperEvidentAuditLog with the policy id and record count.
primitives.extension_contract: Target applications register a policy per data_class and plug in deletion adapters (SQL delete, object-store lifecycle, crypto-shred key destroy). Custom deletion_modes are added by implementing a DeletionAdapter and binding it through the registry.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import timedelta

policy = RetentionPolicy(
    data_class='access_token',
    max_age=timedelta(days=90),
    legal_basis='GDPR Art 5(1)(e) storage limitation',
    deletion_mode='hard',
)
enforcer.bind(policy)
purged = enforcer.sweep()

sources.locator: Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation
Requirement 3.2 — do not store cardholder data beyond retention need
SI-12 Information Management and Retention

primitives.why_essential: Retention without a shared primitive decays into per-table ad-hoc cron jobs that drift from policy; a single binding fixes data-class-to-lifetime across the whole target.
alternatives_considered: Database TTL indexes — only work per collection and ignore legal_basis, legal hold, and deletion_mode.
Cron scripts per table — drift silently when schema evolves and produce no audit evidence.
Leaving retention to ops runbooks — moves the rule outside code review and fails SOC 2 evidence.

primitives.name: ConsentLedger
primitives.purpose: Records granular per-subject, per-purpose consent grants and revocations with timestamp and version of the notice accepted.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol
from datetime import datetime

class ConsentLedger(Protocol):
    def grant(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, notice_version: str, at: datetime) -> str: ...
    def revoke(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, at: datetime) -> None: ...
    def is_granted(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, at: datetime | None = None) -> bool: ...
    def history(self, subject_id: str) -> list[dict]: ...
invariants: Consent MUST be keyed by (subject_id, purpose); a blanket grant across purposes CANNOT be recorded.
Every grant MUST reference a notice_version string so the exact text the subject accepted is reconstructible; missing version SHALL raise.
Revocation MUST be as easy as grant and SHALL take effect immediately; future is_granted calls for that (subject, purpose) MUST return False.
History entries MUST be append-only; a revocation NEVER erases a prior grant, it supersedes it in time.
is_granted MUST be evaluated against the state at `at` (or now), not the latest, so audits can reproduce past authorizations.
primitives.extension_contract: Target applications register purposes (e.g. 'marketing_email', 'analytics_profiling') and plug a NoticeVersionProvider adapter. Consent-gated code paths compose the ledger via a policy decorator that blocks execution when is_granted is False.

sources.locator: Article 7 Conditions for consent; Article 6(1)(a) lawful basis

sources.source: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, 2022 revision)

primitives.why_essential: Consent scattered in flags or CRM fields cannot prove lawful basis at a point in time; a shared ledger keeps every grant reproducible and every revocation effective in one place.
alternatives_considered: Boolean column on users table — no history, no notice version, no temporal query.
CRM tool as source of truth — outside the transactional boundary, racy against data processing.
Cookie banner state only — covers web UI consent, not API/backend-initiated processing.

primitives.name: DataSubjectRequest
primitives.purpose: Coordinates the lifecycle of an access or erasure request across all stores that hold data about the subject, with a SLA clock.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Literal
from datetime import datetime

DsrKind = Literal['access', 'portability', 'erasure', 'rectification']

class DataSubjectRequest(Protocol):
    def open(self, subject_id: str, kind: DsrKind, received_at: datetime) -> str: ...
    def attach_artifact(self, request_id: str, store: str, manifest: bytes) -> None: ...
    def close(self, request_id: str, outcome: str) -> None: ...
    def due_at(self, request_id: str) -> datetime: ...
invariants: Every request MUST have a statutory due_at computed from received_at; the clock NEVER pauses for internal delays.
Every registered store holding subject data MUST attach an artifact before close; a request CANNOT close with missing stores.
Erasure requests MUST invoke the ErasureCascade; a close with kind='erasure' and no cascade artifact SHALL be rejected.
Open, artifact, and close actions MUST each emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry for regulator replay.
Access and portability exports MUST be delivered via a time-bound, signed URL; exports NEVER live beyond the delivery window.
primitives.extension_contract: Each data store implements a StoreAdapter (with .collect(subject_id) and .erase(subject_id)) and registers itself. Kind-specific workflow steps are added as plugins that subscribe to the request lifecycle hook.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def handle_rtbf(dsr: DataSubjectRequest, subject_id: str) -> str:
    rid = dsr.open(subject_id, 'erasure', datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    for store in ('users', 'events', 'backups'):
        dsr.attach_artifact(rid, store, b'erased')
    dsr.close(rid, outcome='completed')
    return rid

primitives.why_essential: An ad-hoc ticket per erasure guarantees missed stores and blown deadlines; a primitive forces a closed-loop manifest across every adapter before the request can be marked complete.
alternatives_considered: Support-desk ticket workflow — no programmatic cascade, no SLA enforcement, no audit evidence.
Per-service DELETE endpoints without coordination — impossible to prove completeness to a regulator.
A generic job queue — lacks kind-specific statutory deadlines and artifact manifest.

primitives.name: PiiClassification
primitives.purpose: Schema-level annotation that tags every field as one of PII, PHI, PCI, or public, gating serialization and logging through a central mask.
primitives.api_signature:
from enum import Enum
from typing import Protocol, Any, Mapping

class PiiClass(str, Enum):
    PUBLIC = 'public'
    INTERNAL = 'internal'
    PII = 'pii'
    PHI = 'phi'
    PCI = 'pci'

class PiiClassification(Protocol):
    def classify(self, model: type, field: str) -> PiiClass: ...
    def mask(self, obj: Any, audience: str) -> Mapping[str, Any]: ...
    def audit_leak(self, obj: Any, sink: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Every persisted field MUST carry a PiiClass annotation; fields without one SHALL fail schema registration at import time.
Serializers and log formatters MUST route through mask() before emission; writing a raw object to a sink is FORBIDDEN.
PHI and PCI fields MUST NEVER be emitted to unauthenticated audiences, even masked, unless the field is explicitly PUBLIC.
mask() output for an audience MUST be deterministic so diff tests can assert non-leakage.
Reclassifying a field down the sensitivity ladder (PHI → PII → PUBLIC) MUST require an audit log entry with approver id.
primitives.extension_contract: Frameworks register a schema walker that extracts the annotation and plug an AudienceResolver adapter mapping request contexts to audiences. Custom PiiClass values are added by subclassing the enum and registering a mask policy for each new class.

sources.locator: § 164.514(b) de-identification safe-harbor field list
Requirement 3.4 — render PAN unreadable (masking, truncation, hashing)
MP-3 Media Marking; MP-4 Media Storage

primitives.why_essential: Without a schema-level classifier, every endpoint re-invents masking and one forgotten field leaks an SSN to a log; one central primitive makes leakage a type error, not a code-review catch.
alternatives_considered: Regex scrubbers on log output — lossy, high false-negative rate, cannot tell PHI from PII.
Per-endpoint DTO mapping by hand — drifts when schema evolves, provides no provable coverage.
Storing raw then redacting at export — still leaks to logs, backups, and replication.

primitives.name: AccessLog
primitives.purpose: Records every successful read of classified data with actor, purpose-of-use, and record identifier, distinct from the security audit log.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol
from datetime import datetime

class AccessLog(Protocol):
    def record_read(self, actor: str, record_id: str, data_class: str, purpose_of_use: str, at: datetime) -> None: ...
    def query(self, record_id: str | None = None, actor: str | None = None) -> list[dict]: ...
    def count_by_actor(self, actor: str, since: datetime) -> int: ...
invariants: Every read of a PiiClassification-tagged record MUST emit one AccessLog entry before the response leaves the process.
purpose_of_use MUST be one of a registered set; ad-hoc free-text values SHALL be rejected.
AccessLog entries MUST NEVER be merged with the TamperEvidentAuditLog so high-volume read traffic cannot mask low-volume security events.
Actor MUST be a resolved identity (user, service account, or break-glass id); 'system' without a concrete id is FORBIDDEN.
Retention of AccessLog MUST follow a RetentionPolicy bound at registration; unbounded accumulation CANNOT occur.
primitives.extension_contract: Repositories wrap reads with an access-log interceptor that calls record_read. Custom purpose-of-use codes are added via register_purpose(code, description). Export adapters subscribe to the log to feed HIPAA accounting-of-disclosures reports.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

def read_patient(access: AccessLog, actor: str, patient_id: str) -> dict:
    record = _repo_get(patient_id)
    access.record_read(actor, patient_id, 'phi', 'treatment', datetime.now(timezone.utc))
    return record

sources.locator: § 164.312(b) Audit controls — recording and examining access

primitives.why_essential: Mixing reads into the security audit drowns anomaly detection and breaks HIPAA's accounting-of-disclosures requirement; a separate primitive keeps volumes, retention, and semantics distinct.
alternatives_considered: Single combined audit stream — hides security events under read noise and miscounts for 164.528 disclosures.
Database-level query logging — captures SQL not business actor or purpose_of_use.
HTTP access logs at the proxy — lacks record identity and data classification.

primitives.name: EncryptionPolicy
primitives.purpose: Declares cipher, key provider, and rotation cadence for a data class at rest and in transit, and rejects storage without a bound policy.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EncryptionPolicy:
    data_class: str
    at_rest_cipher: str  # e.g. 'AES-256-GCM'
    in_transit_min_tls: str  # e.g. 'TLS1.2'
    key_provider: str  # kms uri
    rotation: timedelta

class EncryptionRegistry(Protocol):
    def bind(self, policy: EncryptionPolicy) -> None: ...
    def resolve(self, data_class: str) -> EncryptionPolicy: ...
    def require_tls(self, endpoint: str) -> None: ...
invariants: Every data_class that stores PII, PHI, or PCI MUST have an EncryptionPolicy bound; writes without resolve() succeeding SHALL fail.
at_rest_cipher MUST be one of the approved set (AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305); unapproved ciphers SHALL raise on bind.
in_transit_min_tls MUST be TLS1.2 or higher; binding TLS1.0 or TLS1.1 is FORBIDDEN.
key_provider MUST reference an external KMS; raw key material in configuration files is NEVER permitted.
rotation MUST be ≤ 365 days for PCI data_classes; a longer cadence CANNOT be bound.
primitives.extension_contract: Storage adapters register themselves and call resolve(data_class) on every write; TLS-terminating entrypoints register via require_tls(endpoint) middleware. New ciphers are added by extending the approved set through a governance-reviewed registration decorator.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import timedelta

policy = EncryptionPolicy(
    data_class='cardholder_pan',
    at_rest_cipher='AES-256-GCM',
    in_transit_min_tls='TLS1.2',
    key_provider='aws-kms://alias/pci-pan',
    rotation=timedelta(days=365),
)
registry.bind(policy)
resolved = registry.resolve('cardholder_pan')

sources.locator: Requirement 3.5 Protect stored cryptographic keys; 4.2 Strong cryptography in transit
§ 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Encryption and decryption; § 164.312(e)(2)(ii) Transmission encryption
SC-13 Cryptographic Protection; SC-8 Transmission Confidentiality

primitives.why_essential: Per-service encryption choices drift into weak ciphers and hard-coded keys; a single registry makes cipher approval, KMS usage, and rotation cadence enforceable rather than conventional.
alternatives_considered: Trust cloud defaults for disk encryption — does not cover field-level encryption or key ownership.
TLS enforced only at the load balancer — internal hops bypass the rule and leak on VPC peering.
Ad-hoc env var keys — no rotation, no KMS audit trail, violates PCI 3.5.

primitives.name: KeyRotationSchedule
primitives.purpose: Drives rotation of data-encryption keys on a fixed cadence with overlap window, and blocks new writes with a key past its cutover.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KeyRotationSchedule:
    key_alias: str
    cadence: timedelta
    overlap: timedelta
    next_rotation_at: datetime

class KeyRotator(Protocol):
    def schedule(self, sched: KeyRotationSchedule) -> None: ...
    def rotate_now(self, key_alias: str) -> str: ...
    def active_key(self, key_alias: str, at: datetime) -> str: ...
invariants: A new key version MUST be produced on or before next_rotation_at; missing a rotation SHALL raise an alert to the compliance channel.
overlap MUST be > 0 so decryption of records written with the prior version NEVER fails during cutover.
active_key() MUST return exactly one current key per alias at any instant; ties or gaps CANNOT occur.
Keys past cadence + overlap MUST be marked decrypt-only; new writes with such keys SHALL be rejected.
Rotation events MUST emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry capturing old and new key versions.
primitives.extension_contract: KMS providers implement a RotationAdapter with .create_version(alias) and .set_primary(alias, version). Target applications register schedules at startup; custom post-rotation steps are added via a rotation hook that runs inside the rotation transaction.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

sched = KeyRotationSchedule(
    key_alias='alias/pii-field',
    cadence=timedelta(days=90),
    overlap=timedelta(days=7),
    next_rotation_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=90),
)
rotator.schedule(sched)
kid = rotator.active_key('alias/pii-field', datetime.now(timezone.utc))

sources.locator: Requirement 3.7.4 — cryptographic key changes at defined cryptoperiod
SC-12 Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management

primitives.why_essential: Rotation done via quarterly runbooks silently lapses; a scheduled primitive turns cadence into code and makes missed rotations a failing build signal rather than an audit finding.
alternatives_considered: Manual rotation via ops playbook — depends on humans and misses under load.
Cloud-managed auto-rotation only — covers CMKs but not application-scoped DEKs or HMAC keys.
Single long-lived key with periodic audit — leaves a long blast radius on compromise.

primitives.name: ProcessingRecord
primitives.purpose: Machine-readable record of processing activities that a controller must maintain, generated from code rather than a separate document.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProcessingRecord:
    activity: str
    controller: str
    purposes: tuple[str, ...]
    data_classes: tuple[str, ...]
    recipients: tuple[str, ...]
    retention_ref: str
    legal_basis: str
    transfers_outside_eea: tuple[str, ...] = ()

class ProcessingRegistry(Protocol):
    def register(self, record: ProcessingRecord) -> None: ...
    def export_ropa(self) -> bytes: ...
invariants: Every code path that reads or writes PII MUST be annotated with a registered ProcessingRecord.activity; unregistered activities SHALL fail at startup.
Each record MUST reference a retention_ref that resolves to a bound RetentionPolicy; dangling refs CANNOT register.
legal_basis MUST be one of GDPR Article 6(1)(a-f); free-text values SHALL raise.
transfers_outside_eea entries MUST be ISO-3166 country codes; other formats are FORBIDDEN.
export_ropa() output MUST be byte-for-byte reproducible given the same registry so auditors can hash and diff releases.
primitives.extension_contract: Frameworks register activities via a decorator on handler functions that emits the ProcessingRecord at import time. Custom export adapters (e.g. OneTrust CSV, JSON-LD DPF) are added by implementing a RopaExporter and binding it to the registry.
primitives.consumption_example:
record = ProcessingRecord(
    activity='user.signup',
    controller='AcmeCorp GmbH',
    purposes=('account_creation',),
    data_classes=('pii_email', 'pii_name'),
    recipients=('internal',),
    retention_ref='retention:user_account',
    legal_basis='GDPR Art 6(1)(b) contract',
)
registry.register(record)

sources.locator: Article 30 Records of processing activities

primitives.why_essential: ROPA maintained as a spreadsheet drifts from the code within a sprint; a registry built from decorators keeps the record synchronized to what the system actually does.
alternatives_considered: Externally-maintained spreadsheet — drifts from reality by definition.
Privacy team interviews every release — lossy, expensive, not reproducible.
Data-flow scanners only — detect flows but cannot assert purpose or legal basis.

primitives.name: LegalHold
primitives.purpose: Suspends retention-driven deletion and erasure cascades for records covered by a litigation or regulatory hold until the hold is released.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LegalHold:
    hold_id: str
    scope_query: str
    opened_at: datetime
    opened_by: str

class LegalHoldRegistry(Protocol):
    def open(self, hold: LegalHold) -> None: ...
    def release(self, hold_id: str, released_by: str) -> None: ...
    def covers(self, record_id: str) -> bool: ...
invariants: RetentionPolicy.sweep and DataSubjectRequest erasure MUST call covers(record_id) before deletion; deletion of held records is FORBIDDEN.
Opening and releasing a hold MUST each emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry with actor and scope.
A hold CANNOT be silently released; release requires a distinct released_by actor from opened_by or an explicit override flag.
Held records MUST remain readable to authorized investigators; indexes SHALL NOT drop held rows.
scope_query MUST be stable against schema evolution; unresolved fields SHALL raise on open rather than silently miss records.
primitives.extension_contract: Storage adapters implement a HoldCheck hook that intercepts delete operations. Target applications extend the registry with custom scope resolvers (e.g. tenant_id = X) by subclassing the scope query evaluator and registering it.
primitives.consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

hold = LegalHold(
    hold_id='case-2024-1138',
    scope_query="tenant_id = 'acme' AND created_at >= '2023-01-01'",
    opened_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    opened_by='counsel@acme.com',
)
registry.open(hold)
assert registry.covers('user:42') in (True, False)

sources.source: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, 2022 revision)
sources.locator: CC2.3 — internal communication about obligations; evidence preservation
AU-11 Audit Record Retention — preservation for investigations

primitives.why_essential: Without an explicit hold primitive, the retention sweeper destroys evidence under active litigation and the erasure endpoint fulfills an RTBF request that should have been paused; one flag cannot carry that logic.
alternatives_considered: A boolean column 'do_not_delete' — no scope, no audit, no release protocol.
Disabling the purge job globally — over-broad, violates retention for unrelated data.
Email-based legal notice to ops — not enforceable in code.

primitives.name: BreachNotificationQueue
primitives.purpose: Tracks suspected and confirmed personal-data incidents with a statutory notification clock, so the 72-hour window is enforced in code.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Literal
from datetime import datetime

Severity = Literal['low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical']

class BreachNotificationQueue(Protocol):
    def open_incident(self, detected_at: datetime, severity: Severity, summary: str) -> str: ...
    def confirm(self, incident_id: str, confirmed_at: datetime, data_classes: tuple[str, ...]) -> None: ...
    def notify_authority(self, incident_id: str, authority: str, at: datetime, reference: str) -> None: ...
    def close(self, incident_id: str, outcome: str) -> None: ...
invariants: An incident confirmed as affecting personal data MUST have a notify_authority call within 72 hours of confirmed_at; the queue SHALL emit a breach-of-SLA alert at T-24h.
open_incident MUST be callable from any service with write access to the queue; there is NEVER a gating step that delays detection recording.
Every state transition (open, confirm, notify, close) MUST emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry.
data_classes on confirm MUST be a non-empty tuple of PiiClassification-registered classes; empty tuples SHALL raise.
An incident CANNOT close without either a notify_authority entry or an explicit 'no_notification_required' outcome with a legal_basis field.
primitives.extension_contract: Detection sources (IDS, anomaly scoring, manual reports) call open_incident. Notification channel plugins (DPA portal adapters, HHS OCR form submitters) subscribe to the notify phase and register themselves as NotificationChannel implementations.

sources.locator: Article 33 notification of personal data breach to supervisory authority within 72 hours
§ 164.308(a)(6) Security incident procedures

primitives.why_essential: Incident trackers in ticketing tools have no statutory clock; a domain-specific queue makes the 72-hour GDPR window and HIPAA incident response requirement computable and alertable.
alternatives_considered: Generic Jira project for incidents — no statutory clock, no authority-notification tracking.
PagerDuty postmortems — operational focus, not regulatory evidence.
Email distribution list — untracked, non-reproducible state.

primitives.name: DataResidencyPolicy
primitives.purpose: Binds a data class to a set of permitted storage and processing regions, refusing writes or cross-border transfers outside the allow-list.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DataResidencyPolicy:
    data_class: str
    allowed_regions: tuple[str, ...]
    transfer_mechanism: str  # e.g. 'SCC_2021/914', 'adequacy_decision', 'intra_group_BCR'

class ResidencyEnforcer(Protocol):
    def bind(self, policy: DataResidencyPolicy) -> None: ...
    def check_write(self, data_class: str, region: str) -> None: ...
    def check_transfer(self, data_class: str, source: str, destination: str) -> None: ...
invariants: allowed_regions MUST be ISO-3166 codes; arbitrary strings SHALL raise on bind.
A write to a non-allowed region MUST fail loudly; silent replication outside the policy is FORBIDDEN.
A cross-border transfer outside the EEA CANNOT proceed without a valid transfer_mechanism reference on the bound policy.
check_write MUST be called before any persistence primitive stores the record; policies enforced only at read time NEVER satisfy residency.
Policy changes MUST emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry so region scope changes are reviewable.
primitives.extension_contract: Storage adapters call check_write before persisting; replication and backup jobs call check_transfer for each destination. Custom transfer_mechanism values are added by registering a TransferMechanism adapter that validates the legal artifact (SCC signed, adequacy decision id).
primitives.consumption_example:
policy = DataResidencyPolicy(
    data_class='eu_user_profile',
    allowed_regions=('DE', 'IE', 'FR'),
    transfer_mechanism='SCC_2021/914',
)
enforcer.bind(policy)
enforcer.check_write('eu_user_profile', region='DE')

sources.locator: Articles 44-50 (Chapter V) transfers of personal data to third countries
Requirement 12.8 — third-party service providers and cross-border processing

primitives.why_essential: Residency implemented as a single config flag misses replicas, backups, and analytics copies; a per-class primitive forces every write-path and transfer-path to prove eligibility against the same registry.
alternatives_considered: Deploy per-region and hope traffic stays put — ignores analytics, backups, and support read-paths.
Network-level geo fencing — breaks on VPN and does not cover application-layer logical copies.
Contractual clauses alone — enforceable against vendors but not against one's own replication jobs.

cross_cutting_insights: Every compliance primitive hangs off TamperEvidentAuditLog: retention purges, DSAR closures, hold open/release, breach notifications, key rotations, and residency policy changes all emit chained entries — one signed stream is the spine.

PiiClassification is upstream of almost every other primitive: AccessLog, EncryptionPolicy, RetentionPolicy, ProcessingRecord, and DataResidencyPolicy all key their behavior on the data_class label, so mis-tagging a field multiplies through the system.

Retention and erasure conflict with evidence preservation; LegalHold is the explicit reconciliation primitive, and without it GDPR Art 17 erasure and NIST AU-11 preservation become contradictory runtime behaviors.

Consent and ProcessingRecord are two sides of lawful basis: consent carries subject-level state per purpose (Art 7), while ProcessingRecord carries controller-level state per activity (Art 30); neither alone proves compliance.

Time is first-class: DSAR due_at, BreachNotificationQueue 72h clock, KeyRotationSchedule cadence, and RetentionPolicy max_age each model a statutory or cryptographic deadline that MUST fire in code, not in runbooks.

Separation of AccessLog from TamperEvidentAuditLog is a volume decision enforced by regulation — HIPAA accounting-of-disclosures (164.528) would be unworkable if every PHI read drowned the security event stream.

Every POLICY-namespace primitive (EncryptionPolicy, KeyRotationSchedule, DataResidencyPolicy) is a registry-bound fail-closed gate: binding is at startup, enforcement is at every write, no runtime escape hatch.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 has no hash-chained audit primitive; writes land in structured logs without per-entry signature or chain verification.
No declarative RetentionPolicy binding exists — retention is per-table, enforced by ad-hoc scripts without legal_basis traceability.
ConsentLedger-like primitive is absent; consent state is modeled as boolean flags without notice-version history.
DSAR/RTBF requires a cross-store cascade; no current primitive enforces that every registered store attaches an artifact before closing a request.
PiiClassification at schema level is missing — masking is left to serializer code, which means a new field ships unclassified by default.
AccessLog separate from the security audit is not provided, blocking HIPAA 164.528 accounting-of-disclosures reports.
EncryptionPolicy per data_class is not enforced at write; at-rest encryption is trusted to cloud defaults without cipher or rotation guarantees.
LegalHold primitive is absent, so retention sweepers can destroy evidence under active investigation.
Breach notification lacks a statutory clock — incidents live in generic tickets with no 72-hour SLA alerting.
DataResidencyPolicy is not modeled; region binding relies on deployment topology and ignores replicas and backups.
